sentences.text: The present application has been filed by the appellant seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

2. By way of present appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement dated 21.11.2023 and order on sentence dated 31.01.2024 vide which he has been directed to undergo RI for a period of 11 years alongwith fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default whereof he would undergo SI for 1 month, for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) IPC.
He was further sentenced to undergo RI for 11 years alongwith fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default whereof he would undergo SI for 1 month, for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n).
All sentences were directed to run concurrently and benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C. was provided to the appellant.

sentences.text: Mr. Pujari, learned counsel for the appellant, states that though the prosecution has alleged that the victim is a minor, her age has not been conclusively proved.
He submits that suggestions were put to the victim to the effect that she was a major and that she had gone and resided with the appellant for a period of 15 months of her own accord.
He further submits that there exists variance between the various statements of the victim and her testimony before the Trial Court.
Whereas in her Court deposition the victim stated that she became pregnant and the foetus was aborted no such allegation was made in her statements during the investigation.
The I.O. also did not carry out any investigation or collect any documentary proof in this regard.
He further submits that though the MLC of the victim was placed on record, it is not suggestive of any offence of rape.
It is stated that the FSL report also does not connect the appellant with the crime.
Lastly, it is submitted that the appellant has undergone about 5 years of incarceration out of the sentence of 11 years imposed upon him.

4. The present application is opposed by the learned APP for the State, who states that the age of the victim was proved through her birth certificate, which was admitted by the appellant under Section 294 Cr.P.C.

It is further submitted that the victim's testimony clearly establishes the offence and since the victim is a child, the question of consent does not arise.
5.
In rejoinder, Mr. Pujari states that under Section 294 Cr.P.C. the appellant had only dispended with the formal proof of the birth certificate and had not admitted the contents thereof.
The said submission is denied by the learned APP.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/09/2025 at 23:19:40 hearing of the appeal is likely to take some time, the sentence of the applicant/appellant is directed to be suspended during the pendency of the present appeal, subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.10,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court/Duty Judicial Magistrate/Link Judicial Magistrate/Jail Superintendent and also subject to the further following conditions:-
(i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer, as well as to this Court.
(ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
(iii) The appellant will not get in touch directly or indirectly with the victim.
(iv) The appellant shall also provide his contact number to the I.O. and shall remain available on that number.
